subject: Short-term concurrency window and reconciliation path
messages:
From: Emily Stone <emily@nimbusretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch spike — request for short-term concurrency window and estimate

Mina,

We're going live with a targeted marketing push next week and our internal load tests show a concentrated burst in a ~48–72 hour window. We ran the numbers and expect traffic to ramp from our baseline (200 QPS) to peaks around 1,100–1,300 QPS for short periods.

Can Redwood provide a temporary concurrency increase for that window? Specifically we'd like:
- A 72-hour uplift to support up to 1,200 QPS
- Clear metering so we can reconcile exact token consumption post-window
- A proposed blended price for the uplift and any overrun true-up mechanics

I'm including our forecast as an attachment (launch_traffic_forecast.xlsx). Procurement (procurement@nimbusretail.com) is on copy — we can expedite a PO if terms are clear.

High level asks: what are our options for a time-boxed uplift, and what credit/true-up paths do you offer if we exceed the provisional allowance?

Thanks,
Emily Stone
Head of Platform Operations
Nimbus Retail

-- attachment: launch_traffic_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, procurement@nimbusretail.com
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch spike — request for short-term concurrency window and estimate

Emily — thanks for the detail and the forecast. We can support a short-term concurrency window; below are two practical paths depending on how Nimbus wants to balance speed vs. cost certainty.

Option A — Short window uplift (fastest):
- 72-hour uplift to 1,200 QPS (provisioned capacity)
- Temporary blended uplift rate (tokens served during window billed at uplift rate)
- Automatic fall-back to baseline after window; engineering toggle we can coordinate

Option B — Provisional allowance + overrun true-up (lower upfront cost):
- Provide a provisional allowance (e.g., 500k extra tokens per day) at a discounted uplift rate
- Overrun beyond allowance billed at standard overrun rate with a 10% provisional credit applied to the first invoice after true-up

Either path includes:
- Detailed metering logs and a reconciliation report within 5 business days of window close
- A one-time launch credit we can offer subject to sign-off (details in attached provisional_uplift_quote.pdf)

Next steps: if you want Option A we can provision capacity immediately once we have a signed DocuSign and a PO. Option B requires a short SOW amendment + PO. I've attached a one-page quote with numbers and the draft temporary_terms docx.

Ben — can you add the standard uplift appendix and DocuSign link?

Mina
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

-- attachment: provisional_uplift_quote.pdf (quote)
-- attachment: temporary_concurrency_terms.docx (terms draft)
From: Emily Stone <emily@nimbusretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@nimbusretail.com>, procurement@nimbusretail.com
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch spike — request for short-term concurrency window and estimate

Thanks Mina — Option A looks like the simplest for the timeline. We want to avoid engineering churn during the launch, so provisioning is preferred over having to manage allowances mid-run.

Quick clarifications:
- Metering: will the reconciliation report include token-level breakdown by route/model? We need that to match our internal billing.
- Credit: what triggers the one-time launch credit? Is it conditional on signing before the launch window?
- IP & rate-limits: can you loop in the infra lead who will coordinate the temporary rate-limit and any IP allowlists if needed?

Procurement is ready to issue a PO once we have the DocuSign and final uplift figure.

Emily

Emily — following up with the agreed terms and next steps. Forwarding the quote and the DocuSign envelope for signature.

Summary (final):
- Provisioned uplift: 72 hours starting at the time you confirm go-live (up to 1,200 QPS).
- Billing: uplift traffic billed at a temporary blended per-token uplift rate (see DocuSign quote). Any consumption beyond provisioned capacity during the period will be billed at overrun rate; we will apply a one-time launch credit of 15% to overrun charges in the first invoice after reconciliation.
- Metering & reports: per-route token breakdown + per-model aggregation provided in CSV within 5 business days.
- Reconciliation: Redwood will send a reconciliation PDF and raw CSV; Nimbus confirms token counts and we issue an adjustment invoice if required.
- PO/Execution: sign the DocuSign (link below) and send us the PO; once both are received we will schedule the provisioning window with Infra (we can flip the switch within 2 hours of confirmation).

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/NDX-3928
